_readme: This is the whole dictionary. Add a word by adding an object to "terms" and running: python3 build.py. Fields: term (required), aka, definition (string or list of paragraphs), plainly, tags, seeAlso, emoji, post (the URL of the LinkedIn post that introduced this specific term, shown on its term page; must match one of the URLs in that letter's "posts" list). "posts" maps a letter to the LinkedIn post(s) announcing it, shown as link(s) on that letter's page. Value can be a single URL string or a list of URL strings for multiple posts.

site.title: A–Z Competition Law Dictionary
site.tagline: Australian competition law, one friendly word at a time.
site.description: A cheerful, plain-English dictionary of Australian competition law terms, published one letter at a time from A to Z.

definition: A legal framework within competition law that allows third-party businesses to use essential infrastructure owned by a competitor on reasonable terms and conditions.
Examples found in rail, wheat export and telecommunications networks.
Otherwise known as the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
Federal regulator of competition and consumer law in Australia.
Otherwise known as the Australian Consumer Law.
Federal legislation for consumer law regulation in Australia - found in Schedule 2 of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth).
All the communications that businesses (and sometimes influencers) use to attract attention to their products and services, with the goal of maximising customer conversion and revenue.
Key focus area for many misleading or deceptive conduct claims.
Often used in overseas jurisdictions including the United States to refer to the practice of competition law.
Refers to rules and laws that promote fair competition between businesses.
A public pathway involving an ACCC application to protect conduct you are about to engage in that may otherwise contravene competition laws.
Depending on the conduct, you need to prove either: 1. the conduct is not likely to substantially lessen competition; or 2. the conduct is likely to result in a net public benefit.
